newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran Sirri oil project moving forward - NIOC.
newsitem.headline: Iran Sirri oil project moving forward - NIOC.

text.p: Total SA's Sirri E and A Iranian oil and gas field development is on schedule with first oil due by end 1997, an Iran oil manager said Saturday.

"Project progress is according to the program, more than 10 percent...Sirri A production will start by the end of 1997 and in Sirri E by the end of 1998," said Seyed Jalilian, director of National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) Offshore.
Production capacity of the fields has been estimated at around 120,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Total signed a groundbreaking $600 million deal with NIOC to develop the two Sirri fields in July 1995.
The French firm secured the contract after U.S. President Bill Clinton barred Houston-based Conoco Inc from carrying out the project.
"Delineation drilling is completed and fabrication of well platforms will soon begin (in the southern Iranian port of Bandar Abbas)," Jalilian told Reuters in an interview.
Jalilian confirmed press reports that the estimate of total recoverable reserves at the two fields had been increased after seismic activity last year.
"Now we are seeing more oil in place but I cannot say the exact figures until after the study," Jalilian said.

The Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter last year reported unofficial estimates that the two fields could hold recoverable reserves as high as one billon barrels, nearly double initial expectations.
